title: Electric field strength — the principle of superposition of fields
printed_title: 67. Electric field strength — the principle of superposition of fields

prose.text:
Electric charge is a property of matter that affects electric pushes and pulls.
An electric field describes the electric push or pull that a charged object would experience at each place.

The idea of an electric field developed gradually through experiments on how charged objects affect one another.
Electrodynamics, the study of electric and magnetic interactions, reveals further properties of fields.
prose.source_text: 电场是什么的概念，是在实验研究电场性质的过程中形成的. 随着电动力学的研究，我们将认识新的内容和电场的新的性质.

prose.text:
An electric field can exert an electric force, a push or pull, on a charge.
Measuring that force at different places helps us discover the field and how it varies from place to place.
A single force measurement does not reveal every property of the field.
prose.source_text: **电场的主要性质是它对电荷施以力的作用** 根据对电荷的作用，人们断定了电场的存在，以及它在空间中的分布，并研究了它的全部特性.

prose.text:
A **reference frame** is the viewpoint from which positions and motion are described.
In a chosen reference frame, a field produced by charges that are at rest and whose arrangement does not change with time is an **electrostatic field**.

A time-changing electric field can be related to changing charge arrangements or magnetic fields.
It is not wholly unrelated to charges or other fields.

Electrostatic fields and alternating fields, fields that repeatedly change with time, can both exert electric forces.
Changing fields also involve time dependence and **electromagnetic induction**, in which a changing magnetic field produces an electric field.

This lesson's electrostatic conclusions do not automatically apply to every changing field.
When discussing properties they share, we can call both kinds electric fields.
prose.source_text: 静止电荷的电场叫做**静电场**. 电场存在于电荷周围的空间中，并与电荷有密切的联系. 今后我们还要介绍与电荷没有密切联系的随时间变化的**交变电场**. 但是，交变电场对电荷的作用，完全与静电场一样. 静电场和交变电场在许多性质方面是一样的. 然而，它们之间也有差异. 谈到场的性质时，如果这个性质完全是**静电场或交变电场**所固有的，则我们把这个场简称为电场.

prose.text:
**Electric field strength** describes the electric force at a chosen place.
A **test charge** is a small charged object used to probe a field.

It must be small enough that its size and its disturbance of the original charge arrangement can be ignored.
Otherwise its force would describe a field changed by the probe itself.
Here the test charge is approximately at rest, and we consider its electric force.
prose.source_text: **电场强度** 电场是根据对电荷的作用力来发现的. 可以断言：如果我们知道了场中任意点对任意电荷的作用力，那么我们就了解了电场.

prose.text:
Call the test charge at the chosen position $q$.
When comparing test charges there, keep the field and the charges producing it unchanged.

A **vector** describes both size and direction, like an arrow showing a push.
The arrow over a letter marks a vector.

By Coulomb's law (8-9), the electric force vector is proportional to $q$.
For test charges with the same sign, multiplying the charge amount by a factor multiplies the force size by that factor.

Dividing the electric force vector on test charge q by its signed charge q gives a result independent of which suitable test charge we use.
A signed charge amount includes its positive or negative sign.

In the next formula, F with an arrow names the electric-force vector.
An equality sign says that the expressions on both sides describe the same quantity.

A fraction bar means divide the quantity above it by the quantity below it.
Read the formula as: field-strength vector equals electric-force vector divided by signed test charge.

This vector is the **electric field strength**, written $\vec{E}$:
prose.source_text: 如果把几个不大的带电体分别放在场中的同一点，并测量力，则发现：电场对电荷的作用力与电荷的电量成正比. 实际上，场是点电荷产生的. 根据库仑定律(8-9)，对置于场中的电荷$q$的作用力，与电荷$q$成正比. 因此，电场对场中某点的电荷的作用力与电荷电量的比值，与电荷的电量无关，从而可以作为场的一个特性. 人们把这个特性叫做**电场强度**. 象力一样，电场强度是一个矢量. 用字母$\vec{E}$表示它. 根据定义

prose.text:
Electric field strength is a vector: the electric force vector on a test charge divided by its signed charge amount.
The test charge must not be zero, because division by zero is not defined.
The electric force in this definition excludes gravity and other forces.
prose.source_text: **某一点的电场强度等于电场对点电荷的作用力与电荷电****量的比值，是一个矢量.**

prose.text:
Once the field strength at a position is known, the electric force on charge $q$ there is:
Writing the charge and field-vector symbols next to each other means multiplication.

Read the following equation as: electric-force vector equals charge multiplied by field-strength vector.
Doubling a suitable test charge doubles its electric force while the original field stays unchanged.
prose.source_text: 由此得出，电场对电荷$q$的作用力等于

prose.text:
The following direction comparisons apply when the electric field is nonzero.
In the formulas, greater than zero means positive, and less than zero means negative.

When $q>0$, $\vec{E}$ and $\vec{F}$ point in the same direction.
When $q<0$, the electric force points opposite to the field strength.

The direction of $\vec{E}$ is defined as the force direction for a positive test charge.
It does not change when the sign of test charge $q$ changes.

If field contributions completely cancel, the field and the electric force are zero.
There is then no direction arrow to assign to either zero vector.
prose.source_text: **如果$q>0$**，则矢量$\vec{E}$和$\vec{F}$的方向相同；当$q<0$时，这两个矢量的方向相反. 矢量$\vec{E}$的方向与电荷$q$的符号无关. 它的方向是电场对正电荷作用力的方向.

prose.text:
Equation (8-11) gives the SI unit of field strength as newtons per coulomb.
SI is the International System of Units;

a newton measures force and a coulomb measures charge.
Newtons per coulomb describes how much electric force acts for a given charge amount.

Per coulomb means the electric force scaled to one coulomb of positive test charge.
This is a way to express the field strength, not an instruction to insert a probe large enough to disturb the source.
In the same unchanged field, doubling a suitably small test-charge amount doubles its force, leaving the force per coulomb unchanged.
prose.source_text: 根据(8-11)式，电场强度的单位在国际单位制中是牛顿/库仑.

prose.text:
**The field of a point charge**
A **source charge** produces the field being studied.

A **point charge** is modeled at a single location because its size is small enough to ignore at the distances considered.
Model source charge $q$ this way, and choose a positive test charge $q_0$ that does not noticeably disturb it.

The lower zero in the test-charge symbol is a label distinguishing it from the source charge;
it does not make the test charge zero.

The following formula uses vacuum or an ideal insulating **dielectric medium**, material whose charges do not flow freely as they can in a conductor.
In a dielectric, bound positive and negative charges can shift slightly in response to an electric field.

This small separation of bound charges is the material response described here.
The medium is **homogeneous**, having the same relevant properties throughout, and **isotropic**, having the same response in every direction.

Its response is **linear**, meaning that multiplying the applied field by a factor multiplies the material's response by that factor.
The model ignores the material's edges, the charged objects' sizes, and small-scale local effects.
Keep the material's state and electrical response properties unchanged.

In the formula, F is the force size and r is the distance from the source charge.
Bars around a charge symbol mean its **absolute value**, its size without the positive or negative sign.

The squared distance means the distance multiplied by itself.
The circle constant pi is the ratio of the distance around a circle to the distance straight across its center.

Epsilon with a lower zero is the vacuum electric constant.
Plain epsilon is the medium's **relative permittivity**, a unit-free factor describing its electric response compared with vacuum.

Vacuum has relative factor one.
For the same fixed source charge and distance in this ideal model, a larger relative factor reduces the field size by that factor.

Vacuum means space without material.
Use charge amounts in coulombs, distance in metres, and the matching SI vacuum constant.
The force size in SI units is:
prose.source_text: **点电荷的电场强度** 我们求点电荷$q$所产生的电场强度. 根据库仑定律，这个电荷对另一电荷$q_0$的作用力在国际单位制中等于

prose.text: $F=\frac{|q|\cdot|q_0|}{4\pi\varepsilon_0\varepsilon r^2}$.
prose.source_text: $F=\frac{|q|\cdot|q_0|}{4\pi\varepsilon_0\varepsilon r^2}$.

prose.text:
At distance $r$ from the source, calculate the field strength size from the test charge's force size.
We are still using a positive test charge, so we can divide directly by its positive charge amount.

For a negative test charge, calculating the size requires division by the charge's absolute value, not its negative signed value.
In the next equation, E without an arrow is the nonnegative size of the electric-field vector.

Read it as field size equals force size divided by the positive test-charge amount.
Substituting the force formula cancels that same positive probe amount, leaving a result determined by the source charge, material, and distance.
prose.source_text: 离产生电场的点电荷距离为$r$处的电场强度的大小等于

prose.text:
$E=\frac{F}{q_0}=\frac{|q|}{4\pi\varepsilon_0\varepsilon r^2}$.
(8-13)
prose.source_text: $E=\frac{F}{q_0}=\frac{|q|}{4\pi\varepsilon_0\varepsilon r^2}$. (8-13)

prose.text:
When $q>0$, the field points straight outward, away from source $q$.
When $q<0$, it points straight inward, toward source $q$, as Figure 113 shows.
prose.source_text: **如果$q>0$**，则电场中任意点的电场强度的方向是沿着半径背向$q$；**如果$q<0$**，则电场强度的方向是沿着半径指向$q$(图113).

prose.label: 图113

prose.label: 图114

The original book also gives CGSE, the older centimetre-gram-second electrostatic unit convention.
It has its own charge and field units and its own conventions for constants.

Changing the measuring unit changes the numerical expression of the same physical quantity.
Its charge and field units and its conventions for constants differ from SI.

Do not mix numbers expressed in these different unit systems.
Under the same ideal insulating dielectric or vacuum conditions, the point charge's field strength size is:
prose.source_text: 在静电单位制中，点电荷的电场强度

prose.text:
$E=\frac{|q|}{\varepsilon r^2}$.
(8-14)
prose.source_text: $E=\frac{|q|}{\varepsilon r^2}$. (8-14)

prose.text:
**The superposition principle**
Keep the positions and amounts of source charges $q_1$ and $q_2$ fixed.
Consider their electric forces on test charge $q$ at the same observation point, the place where we study the field.

Calculate the contributions from $q_1$ and $q_2$ separately, calling the forces $\vec{F}_1$ and $\vec{F}_2$.
The subscripts distinguish the contributions from the different source charges.

The **resultant force**, their combined force, is the vector sum, which combines sizes and directions.
It is not generally found by adding the two sizes alone.
For example, opposite pushes partly or completely cancel, while pushes in the same direction reinforce one another.
prose.source_text: **场的叠加原理** 两个电荷$q_1$和$q_2$对点电荷$q$的作用力的合力，等于每个电荷$q_1$和$q_2$的作用力$\vec{F}_1$和$\vec{F}_2$的几何和.

prose.text: Use the relation between electric force and field strength for each contribution:
prose.source_text: 因为

prose.text: $\vec{F}_1=q\vec{E}_1$ and $\vec{F}_2=q\vec{E}_2$,
prose.source_text: $\vec{F}_1=q\vec{E}_1$ 和 $\vec{F}_2=q\vec{E}_2$，

prose.text:
Here $\vec{E}_1$ and $\vec{E}_2$ are the fields from source charges $q_1$ and $q_2$ at the same observation point.
In vacuum or the linear electrostatic medium model, vector addition of the forces gives:
The same test-charge amount multiplies each field contribution.

We can therefore add the field vectors first and multiply their sum by that common charge amount.
The parentheses in the following expression group the field contributions to be combined.
prose.source_text: 式中$\vec{E}_1$和$\vec{E}_2$是电荷$q_1$和$q_2$产生的电场强度，所以，

prose.text: $\vec{F}=q\vec{E}_1+q\vec{E}_2=q(\vec{E}_1+\vec{E}_2)$.
prose.source_text: $\vec{F}=q\vec{E}_1+q\vec{E}_2=q(\vec{E}_1+\vec{E}_2)$.

prose.text:
Therefore the vector sum $\vec{E}_1+\vec{E}_2$ at test charge $q$ gives the total field strength $\vec{E}$, as Figure 114 shows.
The parallelogram in the picture is a four-sided shape whose opposite sides are parallel, running in the same direction.

It shows how vectors are added at a single point, not a path followed by a charge or test particle.
Keep both component arrows' tails at the observation point.

From each arrow tip, draw a copy of the other arrow, preserving its length and direction.
The copies meet at the far corner.

A **diagonal** joins opposite corners of a four-sided shape.
The resultant is the arrow from the original shared tail to this far corner:
prose.source_text: 从这个等式可以得出：应当把几何和$\vec{E}_1+\vec{E}_2$**看做为电荷$q$****所在的点的合电场强度**$\vec{E}$(图114)：

prose.text: $\vec{E}=\frac{\vec{F}}{q}=\vec{E}_1+\vec{E}_2$.
prose.source_text: $\vec{E}=\frac{\vec{F}}{q}=\vec{E}_1+\vec{E}_2$.

prose.text:
Combining the source fields by vector addition at the same point is called the **superposition principle**.
Dividing the combined force by the common nonzero test-charge amount removes that shared multiplier.
What remains is the sum of the field contributions, not a field that depends on the probe.
prose.source_text: 这就是场的**叠加原理**.

prose.text:
The same method applies to several given sources in vacuum or the linear electrostatic model above.
If their individual field strengths at a single position are $\vec{E}_1$, $\vec{E}_2$, $\vec{E}_3$, and so on, the total is:
prose.source_text: 在一般情况下，叠加原理表述为：**如果几个不同的带电****粒子在空间某一点产生的电场强度分别为$\vec{E}_1$、$\vec{E}_2$、$\vec{E}_3$等等，则****在该点的合电场强度等于**

prose.text:
Superposition says that, in the applicable linear electrostatic model with a given arrangement of source charges, the total field is the vector sum of the source contributions.
It does not mean that charged objects do not interact.

They can still experience forces and move.
Charges in a **conductor**, a material in which charge can move readily, may also rearrange.
When the source arrangement changes, recalculate the field using the new arrangement.

For fixed point charges satisfying the conditions of equation (8-13), first find each charge's field at the chosen position, then add the vectors.
Do not directly apply this rule to a nonlinear medium, whose response does not scale in the simple way described above.
The point-charge field formula is not defined at the source charge's own position, where its distance would be zero.
prose.source_text: 叠加原理表明：当几个电场放在一起时，它们彼此不产生任何影响. 由于有了叠加原理，所以为了求带电粒子系统**在任意点的**电场强度，只要知道点电荷电场强度的表示式(8-13)就是够了.
